description: Classification catalog. Anything not matched here is reported as 'Review' and is never auto-selected — an unrecognised program is a decision for you, not a guess for the tool.

bloat.reason: News feed app. Fetches content in the background.
Weather app with a background refresh task.
Office promotion shell, not Office itself.
Bundled game with ads and a background service.
Windows Mixed Reality portal. No headset, no purpose.
Contacts app tied to the sync services.
Maps app that downloads map data in the background.
Phone Link. Keeps a resident process and polls for a paired phone.
Consumer Teams. Starts with Windows and is a substantial resident process.
New Outlook client with background sync.
Automation tool with a background service.
Xbox title callable UI. Not required for Fortnite, which uses Epic Online Services.
Xbox overlay. Overlays add latency to the present path and can conflict with anti-cheat.
Xbox app / Game Pass client. Fortnite does not use it.
OEM-bundled antivirus trial. Duplicate real-time scanning on top of Defender is a genuine and large performance cost, and the two conflict.
OEM-bundled antivirus trial. Same reasoning as McAfee.
Third-party antivirus. Duplicate scanning and a network filter driver in the packet path.
Generic 'PC booster' utility. These almost universally add overhead rather than remove it.
Third-party driver updaters are a common source of broken drivers. Get GPU and chipset drivers from the vendor.

keep.reason: Runtime that Fortnite and Easy Anti-Cheat link against. Also on the hard protection list.
Runtime used by the Epic launcher and driver tooling.
Chipset, storage and networking drivers for your Z590 board.
You need the Store to reinstall anything removed by mistake. Removing it makes recovery considerably harder.
Provides winget, which is the easiest way to reinstall things later.
Useful for running this tool and any recovery steps.
Framework package that other applications depend on.
Framework package. Removing it breaks Settings and Store UI.
Editing config files without a text editor is unnecessarily painful.
The Windows Security interface. You need this to manage Tamper Protection and Defender settings.
Board vendor utility for your MSI Z590. Marked keep rather than bloat because it exposes fan curves — but if you set fan curves in BIOS instead, this is safe to remove.

Not required, but flagged keep rather than bloat because most players want it. Turn OFF its hardware acceleration and overlay: the overlay injects into the game's present path, which costs latency and is a recurring source of anti-cheat friction.
Capture software. Keep if you record, but be aware that capture consumes exactly the GPU headroom this tool is trying to give back to you.
